newsitem.title: USA: General Mills cites tough comparisons.
newsitem.headline: General Mills cites tough comparisons.

text.p: General Mills Inc said Thursday its lower than expected fiscal 1997 fourth quarter and year-end earnings were due to difficult volume comparisons and a less-favorable sales mix.

"Earnings results for the year clearly did not meet our expectations, due to a very difficult operating environment in the U.S. ready-to-eat cereal category," said General Mills chairman and chief executive officer Steve Sanger.
Earnings for its fiscal fourth-quarter ended May 25, 1997 fell to $0.42 a share from $0.49 in the prior-year period. Sales rose to $1.44 billion from $1.38 billion last year.
For all of fiscal 1997, General Mills reported earnings of $3.00 per share before a charge of $0.18 from an accounting change. In fiscal 1996, the company earned $3.00.
Reported sales for the 52-week period ended May 25, 1997, rose four percent to exceed $5.6 billion.

In the prior year's fourth quarter, unit volume grew 11 percent driven by merchandising programs focused on the company's U.S. Olympic team sponsorship. 1997 fourth-quarter unit volume excluding the acquired Ralcorp brands grew nearly two percent, but did not meet expectations, the company said in a news release.
Earlier this year, General Mills completed the purchase of Ralcorp Holdings Inc's branded ready-to-eat cereal and snack mix businesses for $570 million.
Fourth quarter U.S. cereal volume excluding the Ralcorp brands was down one percent from last year, when Big G cereals posted a nearly 10 percent volume gain, the company said.
